original_record.question:
Which of the shapes below cannot be divided into two trapeziums by a single straight line?
<image1>
original_record.solution: The diagrams on the right show how a rectangle, a trapezium, a regular hexagon and a square can be ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_cd0e3896c5b855fa27a7g-02.jpg?height=90&width=632&top_left_y=874&top_left_x=1238) divided into two trapeziums by a single straight line.  However, when a single straight line cuts through a triangle, the triangle is divided into a triangle and a quadrilateral or, if the line passes through a vertex of the original triangle, two triangles. Hence the shape that cannot be divided into two trapeziums is a triangle.
